title: Japanese White Pine: Ancient Five-Needle Pines You Can Visit
meta_description: One was a shogun's bonsai, planted out after 1408 and clipped into the shape of a ship. Three Japanese white pines mapped, all in Kyoto.
intro: All three of these pines have been shaped by hand for six centuries or more, and all three are in Kyoto. The one beside the pond at Kinkaku-ji was a bonsai in a pot belonging to Ashikaga Yoshimitsu, the shogun who built the Golden Pavilion; after his death in 1408 it was planted out and clipped, generation after generation, into a sailing ship with its bow pointed west toward the Pure Land. Yoshimine-dera's grows almost flat instead of upward, named the playing dragon in 1857 and once fifty metres end to end, until bark beetles in 1994 cost it fifteen. Hosen-in's is the subject of a picture frame garden: you sit on a red felt cushion in a wooden hall and look at it through a doorway. That tree is trained to echo Mount Mikami, a cone shaped peak southeast of the city.
